result:
"Keep on top" is in place: there's a pin button in the title bar, plus `windowManager.setAlwaysOnTop( windowId, enabled )` and a read-only `alwaysOnTop` property on the window. The new and existing JS checks pass. I didn't look at it in a real browser, since that needs wp-env and Docker.

**The contributor guide isn't in this checkout.** The latest commit (`68cb9fd7`) removed `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/` for the no-guidance experiment arm. I didn't pull them back from git history, because that would undo the point of the experiment. Instead I ran what `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs. The changes are uncommitted, with no branch or PR created.

**What changed**
- **Stacking** (`src/window-manager/index.ts`): one shared pass now sets every window's z-index. Windows kept on top get their own layer above all the others, and inside that layer they stack in normal focus order. Focus itself is unchanged, so the focused window can sit underneath a pinned one and still take the keyboard. A child window of a pinned window also stays on top, so it never ends up behind its owner.
- **Window** (`src/window/index.ts`): adds the `alwaysOnTop` property. The window starts pinned if it was opened or restored that way. It also gets an `os-window--always-on-top` class, and the pin button's pressed state stays correct even after the title-bar buttons are redrawn.
- **Pin button**: a new built-in control, `core/keep-on-top`, labelled "Keep on top" with a new `pin` icon. It sits just before minimize. I gave it sort order 8 rather than 5 so that plugin buttons already using order 5 to go first still come first. Themes can reorder or hide it with two new CSS variables.
- **Session**: the flag is saved only for pinned windows. It comes back on reload for both normal and native windows, and `includes/session.php` keeps it when cleaning the saved session. Turning it on or off triggers a session save.

**Checks run**
- `npm run lint`: no errors. The 28 warnings are all existing long-file warnings.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `npm run test:js`: all 532 test files pass, including the new `tests/vitest/window-always-on-top.test.ts` (10 tests covering stacking, multiple pinned windows, turning it off, the pin button, the session snapshot and a reload round-trip). I updated `window-chrome-controls-render.test.ts` for the extra button.
- `php -l` on the two PHP files I changed. I added a PHPUnit test for the session cleaning but didn't run it, since the PHP suite was out of scope.

One thing I noticed but didn't touch: the code that updates the fullscreen button's pressed state looks for `.os-window__btn--focus`, but the button's class is `--focus-tab`. So that state probably never reaches the fullscreen button.
